```{=typst}
#set document(title: "Pingfan Hu - CV", author: "Pingfan Hu")
// === PAGE ===
#set page(
  paper: "a4",
  fill: rgb("#F8F7F0"),
  margin: (top: 0.9in, bottom: 0.5in, left: 1in, right: 1in),
  footer: context {
    set text(size: 8pt, fill: rgb("#666"), style: "italic")
    let updated = datetime.today().display(
      "Updated [month repr:long] [day padding:none], [year]"
    )
    grid(
      columns: (1fr, 1fr, 1fr),
      align(left)[#updated],
      align(center)[Page #counter(page).display() of #counter(page).final().last()],
      align(right)[#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]],
    )
  },
)

#set text(font: ("Optima", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial"), size: 11pt)

// === SPACING ===
// Every vertical gap in the document is one of these five, used by name
// below; nothing adds space by hand.
//   line-gap     between the lines of a paragraph or an entry (the leading),
//                and between a head and what it heads
//   para-gap     between paragraphs, entries and blocks
//   head-gap     above a subsection head, and below a section head's rule
//   section-gap  above a section head
//   rule-gap     between a head's words and its rule
// A block asks for a paragraph's gap below it and only a line's above, so
// the gap after anything is the one it asks for, and a head asks for more
// room above. Typst collapses two neighboring gaps to the larger, so a
// subsection right under a section's rule would take head-gap whatever the
// rule asked; every rule asks for it, so the space under a rule is one size.
#let line-gap = 0.5em
#let para-gap = 0.7em
#let head-gap = 1em
#let section-gap = 1.8em
#let rule-gap = 0.4em
#set par(leading: line-gap, spacing: para-gap, justify: false)
#set block(above: line-gap, below: para-gap)

// === LISTS ===
// a bullet is a short gray hairline, a number gray Maple Mono with its
// period, as on the site; each item is an entry, so items stand a
// paragraph apart
#let list-mark = box(height: 0.66em, width: 0.5em, place(horizon, line(length: 0.5em, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#A3A096"))))
#let enum-mark(n) = text(font: "Maple Mono NF", size: 0.8em, fill: rgb("#77746B"))[#n.]
#set list(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.5em, marker: list-mark, spacing: para-gap)
#set enum(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.5em, spacing: para-gap, numbering: enum-mark)

// Navy-blue links
#show link: set text(fill: rgb(0%, 20%, 60%))

// === HELPERS ===
// A mark from the site's glyph map (resources/styles/styles.scss), read at
// compile time so the documents and the page share one drawing: gray, at
// the size of the text, its center 0.29em above the baseline, between the
// lowercase and capital centers, as the page's marks and the skill marks.
#let glyph(name, size: 0.9em) = {
  let scss = read("resources/styles/styles.scss")
  let svg = scss.match(regex("\n  \"" + name + "\": \"(<svg[^\"]*</svg>)\"")).captures.at(0)
  box(width: size, height: 0.58em, place(horizon + center, image(bytes(svg.replace("'black'", "'#77746B'")), height: size)))
}

// Section header with underline rule. Sticky so it never strands at a page bottom.
#let section(name) = block(sticky: true, above: section-gap, below: head-gap, stack(spacing: rule-gap,
  text(size: 12pt, weight: "bold", upper(name)),
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rgb("#888")),
))

// Subsection header - bold, no rule.
#let subsection(name) = block(sticky: true, above: head-gap, below: line-gap,
  text(size: 11pt, weight: "bold", name))

// An aside is a place or a date: gray, tabular figures.
#let aside(body) = text(fill: rgb("#77746B"), number-width: "tabular")[#body]

// An entry: who in bold at the left, the place and the dates gray at the
// right as one run, and the role in italic under who, over its bullets. The
// role has its own line, as at 11pt a role beside the place would wrap. Each
// line is a paragraph, not a grid: a parser that rebuilds a page's columns
// reads a grid's cells column by column, the dates of every entry apart from
// their titles.
#let work-entry(org, role, location, dates) = block(sticky: true, above: head-gap, below: line-gap, stack(spacing: line-gap,
  par[#strong(org)#h(1fr)#aside[#location#h(1em)#dates]],
  par(emph(role)),
))

// === HEADER ===
// A letterhead: who at the left, on the section heads' edge; how to reach
// at the right, flush with the rules' end, each mark closing its line so
// the marks stand in one column. The two sides share a foot.
#grid(
  columns: (1fr, auto),
  align: (left + bottom, right + bottom),
  stack(
    text(size: 22pt)[Pingfan Hu, Ph.D.],
    head-gap,
    [Engineering Management and Systems Engineering \
    The George Washington University, Washington, D.C., USA],
  ),
  grid(
    columns: 1,
    row-gutter: line-gap,
    align: right,
    [Greater Melbourne, Australia~#glyph("map-pin")],
    [Australian Permanent Resident~#glyph("user")],
    [+61 431 251 227~#glyph("phone")],
    [#link("mailto:pingfanhu@proton.me")[pingfanhu\@proton.me]~#glyph("mail")],
    [#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]~#glyph("compass")],
  ),
)

#section[Education]

Doctoral Committee: _John Paul Helveston (Advisor), Caitlin Grady, Johan René van Dorp, & Eric Hittinger_])

#section[Research Interests]

#[
#set list(spacing: line-gap)

- Discrete choice modeling and consumer preferences
- Incentive and program design in energy and transportation
- Electric vehicle grid integration
- Systems modeling: optimization, agent-based and discrete-event simulation (Simio), system dynamics (Vensim), and network analysis
- Survey methodology and open-source research software
- Agentic AI workflows for research software
]

#section[Research Experience]

// an entry's bullets stand a line apart, so they read as one entry
#[
#set list(spacing: line-gap)

#work-entry[The George Washington University][Graduate Research Assistant, Helveston Lab][Washington, D.C.][2023 - 2026]

- Sloan Foundation-funded study of electric vehicle smart charging with UC Davis and UC Irvine, in partnership with Southern California Edison, Pacific Gas & Electric, and National Grid.
- Designed a national choice experiment with 1,356 EV owners and managed its recruitment budget across Meta and Dynata, using A/B tests to find the most cost-effective approach.
- Ran the survey under GW IRB approval (NCR245575) with informed consent.
- Estimated mixed logit models of enrollment: owners value flexibility and recurring payments most, and the models predict uptake for program designs not yet offered.
- Simulated 10,000 EVs, each on its own travel pattern, against CAISO and NYISO load in 55 time-of-use and enrollment scenarios: managed charging cut CAISO peaks by up to 5.6 GW, and moderate enrollment, not maximum, proved most cost-effective.
- Presented findings to stakeholders at the partner utilities and the Sloan Foundation.
- Lead developer of surveydown and sdstudio.

#work-entry[The George Washington University][Student Research Specialist, Professor Caitlin Grady's FEWS Lab][Washington, D.C.][May - Aug. 2023]

- Built a multi-layer network model of the Mid-Atlantic freight system (road, rail, air, and marine) in Python.
- Ranked its nodes by betweenness, closeness, and degree centrality, and measured its resilience under targeted and random node removal.
]
```
